messages:
tanya_sales: Hi @amir_peopleops — I swapped shifts over the holidays and ended up with 4 unused PTO days because of a customer travel freeze Dec 22–27. Our policy mentions a 5-day carryover cap but I saw note about "manager-approved exceptions for operational freezes." Is there a way to carry these forward?

amir_peopleops: hey Tanya, we do have an operational freeze exception for carryover in limited cases. The steps: 1) manager sign-off, 2) Business Ops or Sales Ops confirmation that the travel freeze prevented PTO, 3) People Ops approval. We usually require evidence (calendar block from Ops / internal memo).

dave_manager: I can confirm the travel freeze. I'll upload the Ops memo and approve in the portal. @tanya_sales, please include your PTO request screenshots so auditors can see the intended usage.

hr-bot: People Ops form "Operational Freeze Carryover" posted: https://people.redwoodinference.com/forms/operational-freeze-carryover (auto message).

tanya_sales: Thanks @dave_manager and @amir_peopleops, uploading docs now. Two quick Qs: does the carryover count against the 5-day general cap or is it a separate bucket? Also, will these be auto-approved during year-end adjustments?

amir_peopleops: good questions. For operational freeze exceptions we treat approved days as part of your year carryover but we can make a separate note in the ledger for auditing purposes. It still counts toward the effective cap we can allow, but we have flexibility up to an extra 5 days for operational exceptions in aggregate per employee per year (rare). Approvals are not automatic; docs and manager sign-off are required and we review cases after year-end closes.

tanya_sales: got it — thanks. Filing the portal request now. Appreciate the quick response! :sparkles:

dave_manager: approved in portal.

amir_peopleops: Received. We'll review and confirm by Jan 20. If approved we'll update your leave balance and notify payroll.
